image_style: Full scene composed for a round display: the main action is centered, everything important sits well inside a central circle, and the picture fades smoothly into pure black toward the edges and corners, like a glowing round window floating in darkness. Joyful festive mood, vivid saturated colors, warm glowing light, rich detail, cinematic photorealistic illustration. People have natural happy faces and correct hands.

scenes.title: Día de Reyes
scenes.subject: Día de Reyes in Mexico, evening of January 6, medium shot: a laughing Mexican family around a kitchen table with a colorful embroidered tablecloth; a little boy about seven, wearing a simple flat gold paper crown, jumps up from his chair with both arms raised in joy because he found the tiny white baby figurine in his slice, his grandmother and his teenage sister clap and laugh. In the center a large oval ring-shaped Rosca de Reyes: glossy golden-brown bread with crosswise bands of crackly white sugar crust alternating with thin strips of red, green and yellow fruit paste and red cherries. Brown clay jarro mugs of frothy hot chocolate. Behind them a nativity scene with the Three Kings and colorful papel picado. Warm cozy light.
scenes.motion: The boy jumps up with both arms raised and cheers, the grandmother and sister laugh and clap, the boy bounces happily and points at his slice; steam rises from the hot chocolate.

scenes.title: Escaramuza Charra
scenes.subject: An escaramuza charra performance in a dirt charro arena in golden afternoon light, seen from the side at a medium distance: exactly three smiling Mexican women ride side-saddle on exactly three separate horses, cantering one behind the other in a wide curve with a full horse-length of open space between each horse so every horse is complete and clearly separate, each with one head, one neck and four legs. Each woman rides side-saddle facing forward toward her horse's head, both legs hanging on the horse's left side toward the viewer, her smiling face turned toward the camera. All three wear identical Adelita dresses made of one solid bright fuchsia-pink matte cotton, blouse and skirt the same single color: high closed stand-up collar, short sleeves gathered into a round puff at the shoulder, fitted waist with a sash tied in a butterfly bow and a striped rebozo shawl knotted at the left side of the waist, long full skirt smooth from the waist to the thigh with pleated ruffles only near the hem, draped over the horse's left flank with white starched petticoat ruffles and white pantaloons peeking out above brown leather mid-calf boots. All three wear the exact same ivory-white charro hat of smooth fine woven palm, like a mariachi hat: tall crown pinched with a deep dent in front and creases on the sides, stiff wide brim curling up at the edge, embroidered hatband, thin leather chin strap under the chin. Hair fully pulled back in a low bun at the nape with a pink ribbon bow, no braids. Each holds the reins in her left hand, connected to her horse's bridle and bit, and one long thin plain wooden stick upright in her right hand; matching tooled-leather charro saddles and bridles
scenes.motion: The three riders canter smoothly around the arena in a wide curve, one behind the other with clear space between the horses; the horses' manes and tails flow, the fuchsia skirts and ribbons stream in the wind, the riders smile and lean into the turn; dust rises from the hooves.

scenes.title: Concheros
scenes.subject: Three Concheros (Aztec-Chichimeca dancers) dance energetically in a sunny stone plaza in Mexico City, medium-wide shot, a drummer behind them: each wears a copilli headdress, a tall fan-shaped halo of long natural pheasant tail feathers (tan and brown with dark bars) with a few red and green plumes, rising from a fitted cloth headband with a small beaded sun-disc on the forehead, no metal crown; men are bare-chested with a beaded pectoral collar and a red loincloth (maxtlatl) with long front and back apron panels edged with black-and-gold Aztec step-fret borders and fringe, plus beaded armbands and shin guards; women wear sleeveless red-and-black tunics and knee-length skirts with Aztec step-fret borders, sequins and fringe; all wear dried brown seed-pod ankle rattles (ayoyotes) and leather huarache sandals; dancers hold a gourd rattle in one hand and a small round feather-edged shield in the other; a drummer beats a tall carved wooden huehuetl drum standing on carved feet with a wooden mallet; a seated elder plays a concha, a small mandolin whose rounded back is an armadillo shell; a woman carries a long-handled clay copal censer with swirling smoke
scenes.motion: The dancers stomp and turn in place in a circle, lifting their knees high and spinning slowly, their tall feather headdresses sweeping through the air, ankle rattles shaking; the drummer beats the huehuetl; copal smoke swirls.

scenes.title: Xochimilco
scenes.subject: A long brightly painted trajinera glides on a green Xochimilco canal lined with tall ahuejote trees on a sunny day. The boat is seen mostly from the side and slightly from the front, with the bow toward the left. The boat is narrow, flat-bottomed and wooden, with a squared bow, painted turquoise, red and yellow. One long painted roof on thin posts runs from bow to stern, covering the whole boat. At the very front of the boat stands the portada, fixed to the front end of the roof and spanning the full width of the bow from one side of the hull to the other: a single wide, flat, rectangular wooden signboard facing forward, a little taller than the roof, like a big painted gateway at the front of the boat. A large rounded arch opening is cut through the middle of the board, wide and tall, and you can see into the covered boat through the arch. The arch is framed by bands of rainbow colors, and the board is painted with big flowers and swirling scrolls in red, yellow, green and blue, with no lettering. Under the roof, a long red table runs lengthwise down the middle, with yellow wooden chairs with woven seats on both sides. A smiling family in casual clothes stands up, dancing and clapping along to the music. Four mariachis stand in a row inside the boat under the roof, along the near side, just behind the portada, all fully visible and facing the camera. They wear matching black charro suits: short waist-length jackets, white shirts, big floppy solid red satin bow ties, fitted trousers with a neat row of small silver buttons down each outer leg, and wide tooled belts with silver buckles. Each wears a classic mariachi sombrero de charro of black felt. It has a tall tapered crown with a rounded, pinched and dented top, about as tall as his face, above a very wide stiff brim that curls up slightly at the edge and is trimmed with silver embroidery. Each mariachi holds exactly one instrument: the first a violin and bow, the second a single trumpet, the third a small round-backed vihuela, and the fourth a huge guitarron. The guitarron is an oversized bass guitar with a very deep bulging back and a short neck, held across his belly. At the stern a boatman in a straw hat stands on the back deck holding a long wooden pole with both hands, pushing it into the canal bottom. Colorful flowers decorate the boat.
scenes.motion: The trajinera glides forward along the canal, the mariachis play with energy (the violin bowing, the trumpet raised, the guitars strummed), the family dances and claps, the boatman pushes his pole, the water ripples and sparkles.

scenes.title: Mercado
scenes.subject: A lively traditional Mexican market under colorful canvas awnings: stalls piled with mangoes, oranges, limes, tomatoes, pineapples, strings of dried red chiles and bright flowers. Overhead hang traditional seven-point star piñatas: each has a round center body completely covered in fluffy ruffled fringed pink and purple tissue paper (no disc, no eye), seven cones wrapped in shiny metallic silver, magenta and gold foil, and long fringed tissue-paper streamers hanging from every tip. In front, a smiling tortillera with a dark braid, wearing a white blouse embroidered with colorful flowers and a cotton apron in red-and-white gingham check with a ruffled edge and a front pocket, flips a corn tortilla with her bare fingertips (no spatula, no tongs) on a wide flat thin round black comal griddle resting on a low brazier with glowing coals; beside her on the table a wooden tortilla press with a pressed tortilla in it and a clay bowl of yellow corn masa with masa balls. The corn tortillas on the comal are pale yellow with brown toasted spots, one puffing up. Cheerful shoppers in everyday clothes, warm light.
scenes.motion: The tortillera quickly presses a masa ball in the tortilla press, then flips a tortilla on the comal with her fingertips as one puffs up; shoppers walk past behind her carrying bags, the piñatas sway, steam rises from the comal.

scenes.title: Mariachi
scenes.subject: A mariachi band performs with energy in Plaza Garibaldi, Mexico City, at night under warm plaza lights and papel picado, medium shot of four musicians: Four musicians in matching black gala charro suits: short fitted waist-length jacket with silver-thread embroidery on the lapels, chest and cuffs, tight black trousers with a row of round silver buttons down each outer leg, white shirt, a wide dark wine-red satin butterfly bow tie with two short hanging ends, embroidered belt, black boots. Each wears a black felt charro sombrero: smooth black felt, not straw and not woven palm, a very wide stiff brim with a rolled upturned edge, a tall pinched cone-shaped crown, and rich silver-thread floral embroidery all around the brim and the crown band. Instruments, one each: a clean straight brass trumpet, a violin with its bow, a small five-string vihuela with a rounded back, and a guitarron, a huge deep-bodied fretless bass guitar with a very short neck, a small headstock and a V-shaped back, much bigger and deeper than the guitar. Joyful smiles.
scenes.motion: The mariachis play a lively song: the trumpeter raises his trumpet high and blows, the violinist bows fast, the vihuela and guitarrón players strum hard and sway to the rhythm, one of them shouts a happy grito; they step side to side together.

scenes.title: Jarabe Tapatío
scenes.subject: The Jarabe Tapatío on a festive stage: a charro and a china poblana dance the zapateado around a single black charro sombrero lying on the floor, its tall dented crown and wide brim edged with silver embroidery. The charro is bareheaded with short black hair, nothing on his head; the sombrero on the floor is his, the only sombrero in the scene. He wears a black charro suit: short waist-length jacket and fitted trousers with silver-white scroll embroidery, a single row of round silver buttons down the outer seam of each trouser leg from waist to ankle, white shirt, wide red silk bow tie, black ankle boots. She wears a white short-sleeved blouse with a wide neckline embroidered with bright flowers, a narrow red-white-green striped sash, and a long full flowing skirt in one smooth piece without tiers or ruffles: shiny green satin from waist to hips, the lower part covered in glittering red and multicolor sequins, green hem band. On the front of the skirt, in sequins, the Mexican coat-of-arms eagle exactly as on the Mexican flag: a brown golden eagle seen in side profile, perched on a green nopal cactus, holding a serpent in its beak and talons. Hair in a bun with red flowers and tricolor ribbons, gold earrings
scenes.motion: The couple dances the Jarabe Tapatío: quick stamping zapateado steps, she swings her wide skirt from side to side in big colorful waves and turns around, he dances around her with his hands behind his back, both smiling.

scenes.title: Guelaguetza
scenes.subject: The Guelaguetza festival in Oaxaca: four young women of Tuxtepec dancing the Flor de Piña in a line on an open-air stage with festive decorations, joyful mood. Each wears a different traditional Chinantec or Mazatec huipil as her dress: one loose, straight, boxy tunic hanging from the shoulders to the knee, with no waist sash or belt, short wide sleeves edged in white lace ruffles, densely embroidered over its whole length with big flowers, birds and geometric motifs in red, fuchsia, purple, yellow, blue and green, crossed by horizontal bands of colored satin ribbon and white lace; some huipiles are red with black and white geometric designs, others white with large red embroidered flowers. Below the knee-length huipil only a red striped wrap skirt with a white lace petticoat hem shows, reaching mid-calf. Long black hair braided and wound into a crown of braided multicolored ribbons on top of the head, with long satin ribbon streamers and bows hanging to the shoulders; several strands of red bead necklaces, earrings, many bright bangles on each wrist. They dance barefoot. Each holds one whole pineapple on her shoulder, tied with a red ribbon bow at its crown.
scenes.motion: The dancers dance the Flor de Piña: they step forward and back with quick light steps, sway their hips, swing their huipiles and lift their pineapples high above their heads and back to their shoulders, smiling; their hair ribbons fly.

scenes.title: El Grito
scenes.subject: Mexico City's Zócalo at night on September 15, Independence Day: the Metropolitan Cathedral with two matching grey stone bell towers crowned by bell-shaped cupolas and a central facade section with a clock topped by three small statues; the cathedral is floodlit in the colors of the flag in this exact order from left to right: the left tower glows green, the center of the facade glows white, the right tower glows red; a giant Mexican flag (green stripe at the pole, white with the eagle emblem, red) flies from a very tall, thin plain grey steel flagpole rising straight from a small low base in the middle of the plaza, with no stone obelisk; a cheerful crowd of Mexican families below in everyday clothes with patriotic touches: waving small Mexican flags with three vertical stripes green, white and red, green-white-red face paint on their cheeks, straw sombreros with green, white and red ribbon bands, green Mexico soccer jerseys, tricolor caps and bandanas, a woman wrapped in a striped rebozo shawl, a girl in a white embroidered Mexican blouse, a little boy in a black mariachi suit with a small sombrero; colorful fireworks bursting in the night sky above the cathedral
scenes.motion: The crowd cheers and jumps, waving their flags wildly and raising their arms, fireworks burst one after another above the cathedral, the giant flag waves in the wind.

scenes.title: La Ofrenda
scenes.subject: Day of the Dead at home: a smiling Mexican grandmother and her granddaughter place orange cempasúchil marigolds and light candles on a tall traditional ofrenda altar with several tiers: glowing candles, marigolds, pan de muerto, colorful sugar skulls, papel picado banners, copal incense, fruit and a cup of hot chocolate, no photographs. Warm candlelight.
scenes.motion: The girl places a bunch of marigolds on the altar and the grandmother lights a candle, then they arrange marigold petals together, smiling; candle flames flicker, copal smoke curls up, the papel picado flutters.

scenes.title: Noche de Muertos
scenes.subject: Night of the Dead on Lake Pátzcuaro, Mexico. In the background the rounded hill island of Janitzio glows with hundreds of candles in its hillside cemetery among white houses with red-tiled roofs; on the summit stands a huge, blocky white stone statue of José María Morelos: a man with a cloth tied over his head and a long cape falling to his feet, his right arm raised straight up with a clenched fist, his left hand holding a sword hilt in front of his body. In the foreground, three Purépecha fishermen each stand upright in his own long, narrow, flat-bottomed wooden canoe with low sides and pointed ends, painted turquoise and green with a yellow rim, with a few candles and orange marigolds on the bow. Each man wears a white cotton long-sleeved shirt, loose white cotton trousers, a woven sash, huaraches and a wide flat-brimmed pale palm-straw hat. With both arms raised above his head he holds a long bamboo pole slanting diagonally; lashed to the pole is a wide semicircular hoop of bent wood about three meters across, and from it hangs one enormous sheer net of very fine pale golden thread that falls down to the canoe like a giant translucent funnel or veil, glowing in the candlelight, one huge wing-like net per man. The dark open water reflects the island's candlelight.
scenes.motion: The fishermen raise and lower their huge butterfly nets in slow graceful sweeps like wings opening and closing, the canoes glide forward on the dark water, the candles on the island twinkle and their reflections ripple.

scenes.title: Las Posadas
scenes.subject: Las Posadas at night in a Mexican courtyard: smiling children in warm sweaters, jackets and jeans cheer around a traditional Mexican posada piñata with seven points. The piñata is a round ball covered in ruffled pink tissue-paper rosettes with exactly seven long, smooth, round cone-shaped points, an odd number: one cone points straight up to the rope, one cone points straight down, two cones point to the left, two cones point to the right, and one cone points toward the viewer. Each cone is covered in shiny metallic foil paper in silver, gold, magenta, blue and green, with stacked bands of ruffled multicolored tissue paper at its base and long tissue-paper streamers hanging from its tip. The piñata hangs by its top cone from the middle of a single rope stretched horizontally across the courtyard from wall to wall; one adult at the edge holds the rope's end; no ropes are tied to the side cones. One blindfolded child, a white cloth tied over the eyes, swings a long, straight, plain wooden broomstick of even thickness at it with both hands. Overhead hang strings of colorful papel picado banners and pleated tissue-paper farolito lanterns with warm string lights; red poinsettias in clay pots. Five cheering children stand well apart from each other and a step back from the piñata in a loose semicircle, nobody touching the piñata, cheering and jumping; in the background two children each hold one small lit candle with both hands in front of the chest and one child holds a single sparkler; the children in front raise both open empty hands. Every child has exactly two arms and two hands, no overlapping limbs, and a clear, natural face.
scenes.motion: The blindfolded child swings the stick and hits the piñata, the adult pulls the rope so the piñata jumps up and down, the children cheer, jump and clap, candies and confetti fall from the piñata.
